expected_surviving_bullets: Memantine is an NMDA receptor antagonist approved for moderate-to-severe Alzheimer's disease since 2003.
The drug reduces calcium influx into neurons by approximately 40%.
A 24-week randomized controlled trial enrolled 252 patients with moderate-to-severe Alzheimer's disease.
Memantine treatment led to a 50% improvement in cognitive scores compared to placebo.
The treatment causes meaningful functional stabilization in 65% of participants.
Common adverse effects were dizziness at 7%, headache at 6%, and constipation at 5%.
The evidence indicates that early intervention leads to better outcomes for patients.
